name: The Family & Youth Institute
mission: TO STRENGTHEN AND EMPOWER INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES THROUGH RESEARCH AND EDUCATION THAT PROMOTE: POSITIVE YOUTH DEVELOPMENT, HEALTHY MARRIAGES, EFFECTIVE PARENTING, AND MENTAL HEALTH WELL-BEING.
theoryOfChange: The Family & Youth Institute explicitly states 'the fyi's theory of change' on its website, particularly within its 'Research' section. This framework outlines their community-based participatory research approach, detailing how they partner with communities, engage and integrate community voices, incorporate community perspectives on data, identify practical solutions, and share benefits. Their mission is to strengthen and empower individuals, families, and communities through research and education, with a vision for individuals, families, and communities to thrive, transform, and uplift. Their research process is designed around community participation and empowerment to ensure real-world impact. The organization also mentions an 'Impact Framework' in relation to its 'Neighborhood' initiative.

rich_narrative.summary: The Family and Youth Institute (The FYI) is a research and education organization dedicated to strengthening Muslim families and youth through data-driven insights. <cite id="1">Founded in 2006</cite>, the organization bridges the gap between academic research and community needs by providing resources on mental health, marriage, and parenting. The FYI maintains a <cite id="2">90/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting a high standard of accountability and leadership. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">total revenue of $497,120</cite>, which represents a <cite id="4">42% decline from the previous year</cite>. Despite this revenue volatility, the organization maintains a <cite id="5">program expense ratio of 84.0%</cite>, ensuring that the vast majority of its spending supports its core research and educational initiatives. The organization operates as a capacity builder, focusing on <cite id="6">mental health research and community education</cite> rather than direct clinical services. This model allows them to influence community well-being at scale, though it makes direct cost-per-beneficiary tracking more complex. The FYI is <cite id="7">zakat-eligible</cite>, specifically serving the category of <cite id="8">fisabilillah (in the cause of Allah)</cite> by providing essential knowledge and support systems to the Muslim community.
